title: Discontinuities and One-Sided Behavior
standard_text: P.2L determine various types of discontinuities in the interval (−∞, ∞) as they relate to functions and explore the limitations of the graphing calculator as it relates to the behavior of the function around discontinuities; P.2M describe the left and right-sided behavior of the graph of a function around discontinuities
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets on discontinuities for Texas TEKS P.2L and P.2M: removable, jump and infinite discontinuities, holes, one-sided behavior and calculator limits. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A factor that cancels makes a hole; one that does not makes an asymptote.
key_sub: A jump: the left and right values differ.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A function is continuous at x = c when you can draw through it without lifting your pencil.
  • Removable discontinuity (hole): a factor cancels from the top and bottom.
  • Infinite discontinuity: the bottom is 0 but the top is not (a vertical asymptote).
  • Jump: a piecewise function whose pieces give different values at the boundary. Compare the left and right sides.
  • A graphing calculator may hide a hole or draw a false line at an asymptote.

Examples

Example

f(x) = x2 − 9x − 3

(x − 3)(x + 3) ÷ (x − 3) = x + 3

x = 3 gives 6

Answer: Hole at (3, 6)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling a hole an asymptoteIf the factor cancels, it is a hole.
Giving the hole a y-value of 0Put x into the simplified function.
Trusting the calculator screenCheck the algebra.

items.q: What kind of discontinuity does f(x) = (x + 4)(x − 1)(x + 4) have at x = −4?
items.e: (x + 4) cancels, so the graph is the line y = x − 1 with a hole at x = −4. Removable (a hole).

items.q: What kind of discontinuity does f(x) = x + 3 if x < −1, and f(x) = x + 8 if x ≥ −1 have at x = −1?
items.e: The pieces give 2 and 7 at x = −1: the graph jumps. Jump.

items.q: What kind of discontinuity does f(x) = x + 1 if x < −5, and f(x) = 2x + 6 if x ≥ −5 have at x = −5?
items.e: Both pieces give −4 at x = −5, so the graph is connected there. No discontinuity.

items.q: What kind of discontinuity does f(x) = (x − 5)(x − 2)(x − 5) have at x = 5?
items.e: (x − 5) cancels, so the graph is the line y = x − 2 with a hole at x = 5. Removable (a hole).

items.q: What kind of discontinuity does f(x) = (x − 6)(x − 4) have at x = 4?
items.e: The bottom is 0 at x = 4 but the top is not, so the graph shoots up or down there. Infinite (a vertical asymptote).

items.q: What kind of discontinuity does f(x) = (x − 2)(x − 1)(x − 2) have at x = 2?
items.e: (x − 2) cancels, so the graph is the line y = x − 1 with a hole at x = 2. Removable (a hole).

items.e: The bottom is 0 at x = 1 but the top is not, so the graph shoots up or down there. Infinite (a vertical asymptote).

items.q: What kind of discontinuity does f(x) = x − 1 if x < 2, and f(x) = x − 2 if x ≥ 2 have at x = 2?

items.q: What kind of discontinuity does f(x) = x + 2 if x < −3, and f(x) = x − 3 if x ≥ −3 have at x = −3?
items.e: The pieces give −1 and −6 at x = −3: the graph jumps. Jump.

items.q: Where is the hole in the graph of f(x) = 2x2 + 4x − 6x2 + 10x + 21?
items.e: Factor: 2(x + 3)(x − 1) ÷ ((x + 3)(x + 7)). (x + 3) cancels, leaving 2(x − 1)(x + 7). Put x = −3 into it: −2. (−3, −2).

items.q: Where is the hole in the graph of f(x) = 3x2 − 15x − 18x2 − 3x − 4?
items.e: Factor: 3(x + 1)(x − 6) ÷ ((x + 1)(x − 4)). (x + 1) cancels, leaving 3(x − 6)(x − 4). Put x = −1 into it: 215. (−1, 215).

items.e: Factor: (x + 1)x ÷ ((x + 1)(x + 3)). (x + 1) cancels, leaving x(x + 3). Put x = −1 into it: −12. (−1, −12).

items.e: Factor: 2(x − 3)(x + 1) ÷ ((x − 3)(x − 7)). (x − 3) cancels, leaving 2(x + 1)(x − 7). Put x = 3 into it: −2. (3, −2).

items.q: Where is the hole in the graph of f(x) = 3x2 + 9x + 6x2 + 6x + 8?
items.e: Factor: 3(x + 2)(x + 1) ÷ ((x + 2)(x + 4)). (x + 2) cancels, leaving 3(x + 1)(x + 4). Put x = −2 into it: −32. (−2, −32).

items.q: Where is the hole in the graph of f(x) = 3x2 − 12x − 36x2 − 2x − 24?
items.e: Factor: 3(x − 6)(x + 2) ÷ ((x − 6)(x + 4)). (x − 6) cancels, leaving 3(x + 2)(x + 4). Put x = 6 into it: 125. (6, 125).

items.q: What are the vertical asymptotes of f(x) = x − 2(x + 2)(x − 4)?
items.e: The denominator is (x + 2)(x − 4), which is 0 at x = −2 and x = 4. The numerator is not 0 there, so the asymptotes are x = −2 and x = 4.

items.q: What are the vertical asymptotes of f(x) = x − 2(x + 5)(x − 1)?
items.e: The denominator is (x + 5)(x − 1), which is 0 at x = −5 and x = 1. The numerator is not 0 there, so the asymptotes are x = −5 and x = 1.

items.q: What are the vertical asymptotes of f(x) = x − 2x² − 2x − 15?
items.e: The denominator is (x + 3)(x − 5), which is 0 at x = −3 and x = 5. The numerator is not 0 there, so the asymptotes are x = −3 and x = 5.

items.q: Where is the hole in the graph of f(x) = x + 1x² − 2x − 3?
items.e: (x + 1) cancels, so there is a hole at x = −1. The simplified function is 1/(x − 3); at x = −1 it is −14. The hole is (−1, −14).

items.q: Where is the hole in the graph of f(x) = x + 2x² − 3x − 10?
items.e: (x + 2) cancels, so there is a hole at x = −2. The simplified function is 1/(x − 5); at x = −2 it is −17. The hole is (−2, −17).

items.e: (x + 4) cancels, so there is a hole at x = −4. The simplified function is 1/(x + 5); at x = −4 it is 1. The hole is (−4, 1).
